transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-07-09
Start time: 15:00 PT
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam Patel (Redwood SE), Sofia Ramos (Redwood CSM); Arjun Mehta (BeaconHealth Head of ML), Priya Kapoor (BeaconHealth Platform), Dana Lewis (Security), Tom Ellis (SRE)

Summary:
Quick sync focused on the safety/fallback matrix for cutover, telemetry alignment (golden signals + instrumentation), and a planned soak of the canary. Discussed a mitigations matrix and who owns each rollback/fallback. Agreed next steps include a 24h soak, additional logging hooks, and delivery of SOC2/network diagrams.

Topics covered:
- Canary soak and failure modes
- Fallback matrix (regional fallback, model variant fallback, capacity tier fallback)
- Telemetry: golden signals, traces, synthetic checks, alert thresholds
- Runbook responsibilities and communication paths
- Security checklist for private deployment (KMS, SSO, audit logs)

Transcript:
[00:00:00] Maya: ok good afternoon everyone, thanks for joining on short notice, uh we're here to lock down the safety matrix and telemetry for the pilot cutover, I think we have 45 minutes, so let's go.
[00:00:12] Arjun: thanks Maya, quick context — our execs are pushing a tight window, they want minimal user impact but we cannot exceed the 200ms p95 target or it's a non-starter, so that's kinda the north star.
[00:00:22] Tom: and from SRE side we care about burst handling, and how Redwood will behave under 2x peak qps for short bursts.
[00:00:28] Liam: yeah, so we ran the 12h stress last week, we saw a memory plateau after about 8 hours on the 40k token sequences — might be kv cache blowup — note: the transcription system misheard kv as K-V cash earlier, but it looked like a steady growth, not a crash. We instrumented heap and saw GC spikes, we think it's an LRU cache knob we can tune.
[00:00:48] Priya: when you say kv cache knob, is that per-worker or global? how does that affect prefix caching?
[00:00:54] Liam: per-worker, but there is global behavior because the autoscaler keeps more replicas live if cache hit rates drop; prefix caching is still helpful but the effective memory footprint grows. We recommended a quantized model variant for the canary to reduce RAM and CPU, trade is +2–3% quality delta.
[00:01:10] Arjun: hmm quality delta could be okay if we gate it with an A/B bucket. we can start 5% of traffic on quantized variant then ramp if metrics look good.
[00:01:18] Maya: that's exactly in the fallback matrix: primary route -> hosted high-precision if latency and quality OK; fallback route -> quantized variant in same region; secondary fallback -> route to dedicated reserved capacity; tertiary -> degrade to shorter responses with safety header. we sketched this yesterday in the doc (link: https://app.redwood/s/BeaconHealth/pilot-fallback-matrix)
[00:01:36] Dana: I need to call out security — any time traffic or models move across tiers we need audit events and KMS envelope metadata. Who owns the audit log retention?
[00:01:44] Sofia: Redwood can emit audit events to your SIEM via syslog or S3 collection, we support per-tenant retention controls in Private deployments, and we can push HSM/KMS metadata in the request logs. We'll attach the network diagram and SOC2 artifact.
[00:01:56] Dana: ok please send the SOC2 and network diag, also need an answer on whether keys rotate automatically when we trigger a rollback.
[00:02:02] Liam: keys don't rotate on rollback automatically — key rotation is orthogonal — but we can document the procedure; if you need auto-rotate on rollout we can recommend a pattern using your KMS to pre-authorize key versions.
[00:02:10] Priya: regarding telemetry, what are you treating as golden signals? we need real-time alerts that SRE can action.
[00:02:16] Maya: we propose: 1) p95 latency per-route, 2) error rate (5xx + hallucination classifier alerts), 3) cold-start rate, 4) successful KV cache hit ratio, 5) model quality regression alerts from eval set. Also synthetic playback every 5m for end-to-end.
[00:02:30] Tom: how granular are the traces? can we get per-token timing and the kernel-level op timings?
[00:02:35] Liam: we can surface token-level floors in traces but not every token by default because of cardinality; we expose percentiles and slow-op traces on sample rate. We can add a profiler hook for 1% of requests during the soak.
[00:02:46] Arjun: let's set profiler at 1% for the 24h soak, collect both heap profiles and token latencies.
[00:02:51] Maya: I'll capture that as an action item.
[00:02:54] [00:03:00] (brief cross talk, background noise)
[00:03:12] Priya: another constraint — we need to ensure data residency for any logs that contain PHI. BeaconHealth has a rule to never export PHI outside the eu-west-1 region.
[00:03:20] Sofia: for Private deployment we can keep logs in your S3 in region and provide a passthrough, for Hosted we can redact PII at ingestion but that's not the same as residency.
[00:03:30] Dana: so our ask is: keep audit logs + traces in eu-west-1 and do not cross-replicate to other regions. is that possible?
[00:03:36] Liam: yes — in Dedicated/Private we can configure region-local retention, but hosted default replicates metadata for HA. we'll flag that as a must-have for go-live.
[00:03:44] Arjun: about the rollback triggers — can we list deterministic thresholds? e.g., sustained p95 > 220ms for 5 minutes, error rate > 1% of requests, or model quality drift > 2% on our eval set.
[00:03:54] Maya: agreed. here's the proposed rollback table:
- Immediate rollback: crash / unrecoverable OOM / complete model unavailability
- Automated rollback: p95 > 220ms for 5m OR 5xx rate > 1% for 3m
- Canary rollback: regression on eval set + elevated latency for 10m
- Manual rollback: SRE or product flags due to business impact
[00:04:15] Tom: we also want a regional failover policy. if one region hits the threshold we prefer route to second region with a lower traffic cap before global failover.
[00:04:23] Maya: yes, regional fallback -> model variant fallback -> capacity tier fallback. We prefer not to do full global failover unless necessary.
[00:04:30] [00:04:40] (keyboard clack)
[00:04:45] Priya: for the canary soak — what percentage and ramp timing do you recommend?
[00:04:50] Liam: propose: 2% initial ramp, 2x after 30m if metrics stable, 5% after 2 hours, then 20% if soak looks good over 24h, then final 100% over controlled windows. We'll publish a ramp table in the runbook.
[00:05:04] Arjun: can we add synthetic smoke tests at each ramp step to validate outputs?
[00:05:09] Maya: yes, synthetic checks at every step, plus a 'quality gate' — if our eval harness flags >2% drift we pause the ramp automatically.
[00:05:20] Dana: on the audit path, I want confirmation that every model switch and traffic shift is captured as an auditable event with the operator's identity.
[00:05:28] Sofia: that is supported; we have an event store and can emit with operator principal, timing, and reason. we'll include sample JSON for the audit events in the repo.
[00:05:35] Priya: a small nit — the current dashboard shows token cost per-minute aggregated; can we get per-route token cost and projected monthly burn for the pilot?
[00:05:43] Maya: yes, we can provide a cost projection. AE will follow up with a short model/traffic cost spreadsheet — link to be shared.
[00:05:50] [00:06:00] (brief pause)
[00:06:05] Tom: we had one flaky failure this week where a model variant returned malformed structured output. How does Redwood handle model output contract violations?
[00:06:13] Liam: we have function-calling and structured-output validation hooks — if the validator fails we'll mark as a QA failure and can route to a fallback model or to a synchronous sanitizer. For the pilot we recommend 'fail closed' for structured outputs with high business impact, meaning route to fallback model or return controlled error, not raw output.
[00:06:30] Arjun: ok good.
[00:06:34] Maya: recap on owners: Liam runs the canary soak and will instrument heap/profile and share logs; Priya provides traffic shape and peak QPS; Dana confirms compliance gating and KMS rotation questions; Maya will send pricing and the SOC2 + network diag; Sofia will draft audit-event sample and runbook skeleton.
[00:06:54] Liam: I'll also add a small patch to reduce LRU cache size and test impact on hit-rate; if hit-rate drops below threshold we won't proceed.
[00:07:02] Maya: schedule — we target the soak to start Tuesday 2026-07-13 at 09:00 UTC and run 24 hours, then reconvene Wed to decide ramp. Does that work for Beacon?
[00:07:12] Arjun: yes that's fine.
[00:07:15] Priya: we need a final preflight checklist before the soak — can you share the runbook checklist?
[00:07:20] Sofia: we'll share a runbook with steps: preflight smoke, alerting hooks, rollback triggers, communication channels, SSO/SAML test, KMS confirmation, synthetic checks. link: https://app.redwood/s/BeaconHealth/pilot-runbook (will send after call).
[00:07:35] [00:07:40] (murmurs)
[00:07:45] Dana: one last compliance ask — we need an on-call contact list and a timeline for audit log delivery if we request historical events.
[00:07:53] Maya: we'll include a 24/7 on-call rota for Redwood team during the soak and an SLA for log exports (48h for ad-hoc exports).
[00:07:59] Arjun: sounds good.
[00:08:02] Maya: ok any final questions?
[00:08:05] Tom: none from me.
[00:08:07] Priya: none.
[00:08:09] Dana: no.
[00:08:12] Maya: great; action items and next steps noted — we'll send the SOC2 + network diagram and the runbook link within 48 hours. Plan: 24h canary soak starting 2026-07-13 09:00 UTC. We'll reconvene for a 30-minute sync on 2026-07-14 to decide ramp.
[00:08:28] Maya: thanks everyone, end of call.

Notes on transcript quality: medium — some technical terms mis-transcribed (KV cache as K-V cash), occasional speaker label noise.
